notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held text of EO 9699 (four paragraphs: re-establishing the Office of Economic Stabilization with its former functions, re-establishing the Economic Stabilization Board, continuing prior actions, amending conflicting orders) and the held acting texts EO 9762 and EO 9801. Neither ends the order. EO 9762 (1946-07-25) transfers the Office of Economic Stabilization, its functions and the Board to the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion and keeps prior actions in effect: a transfer, not an abolition. EO 9801 (1946-11-09) terminates wage and salary controls under the Stabilization Act of 1942; the 1989 codification row calling 9699 terminated by 9801 is editorial, and 9801 does not mention the Office or the Board. A later order held in the corpus but not frozen in this packet, EO 9809 (1946-12-12), consolidates the Office of Economic Stabilization into the Office of Temporary Controls and terminates the Economic Stabilization Board, which may end clauses 1 and 2 but needs its own reading (consolidation versus termination), and the fate of the Office of Temporary Controls is not frozen either. No clause-by-clause end for all four paragraphs can be sourced from the packet evidence, so no status is recommended.
